key_insight: An interpretable recommender that leverages the inherent structure of psychometric data can produce transparent, risk-aware recommendations suitable for gerontological primary care, improving clinician trust and actionable use.
problem_solved: Overcomes barriers to clinical recommender adoption—scarce public clinical data, opaque black‑box outputs, and lack of clear risk/uncertainty information—by producing explanations tied to psychometric questionnaire structure.
method: Leverage psychometric structure (items, subscales, domains) to constrain and inform the recommendation model so outputs align with clinically meaningful constructs.
Generate human‑readable rationales that map specific questionnaire responses to recommended actions, enabling clinician interpretability and auditability.
Incorporate uncertainty/risk awareness into recommendations to prioritize safe, actionable suggestions for gerontological primary care.
impact: Makes recommendation systems more practical and trustworthy for healthcare settings, helping AI/ML practitioners design models that clinicians can understand, evaluate, and safely act on—especially in geriatrics where risks and interpretability are critical.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: psychometric questionnaire → structured model (domains/items) → interpretable recommendation + rationale
Example patient vignette card showing questionnaire highlights, recommended actions, and the human‑readable explanation
Risk/uncertainty visualization (heatmap or confidence bars) linked to each recommendation
Side‑by‑side comparison chart: interpretable, psychometrics‑aware model vs. black‑box recommender (accuracy vs. explainability)
paper_title: An Interpretable Recommendation Model for Psychometric Data, With an Application to Gerontological Primary Care
paper_authors: Andre Paulino de Lima, Paula Castro, Suzana Carvalho Vaz de Andrade, Rosa Maria Marcucci, Ruth Caldeira de Melo
